title: Rav Yosef bar Abba

paragraphs: Rav Yosef bar Abba. In [Bava Batra 144b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.144b.13-145a.1) Rav Yosef bar Abba reports a teaching that Mar Ukva gave in Shmuel’s name. In [Ketubot 74a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.74a.11), Rav Yosef bar Abba reports a teaching that R’ Menachem gave in R’ Ami’s name. In [Berakhot 59b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.59b.16), he speaks in R’ Yochanan’s name (though in [Rashbam on Pesachim 101a](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashbam_on_Pesachim.101a.10.2) the text is copied simply as 'Rav Yosef'); and in Berakhot 53b, he speaks in Rav’s name (according to the reading of the Rif and the Rosh). Hyman describes him as already a leading figure of the generation in the time of Rav Sheshet,

as in [Avodah Zarah 50a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.50a.12-50b.2), where Rav Yosef bar Abba reports a visit from Rabbah bar Yirmeya, who brought a teaching (מתניתא) with him—'and there is no carpenter or son of a carpenter who can resolve it.' Rav Sheshet said, 'I am no carpenter—yet I will resolve it for him.' And in [Eruvin 7b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.7b.3) Rav Sheshet said to Rav Shmuel bar Abba, and some say to Rav Yosef bar Abba, 'Let me explain it to you.' And in [Bava Kamma 112b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.112b.8) Hyman says the text mistakenly has R' Yosei bar Avahu and should read bar Abba.[^5]

In [Bava Metzia 72b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.72b.15), Rav Yosef bar Chama (father of Rava)—and some say Rav Yosef bar Abba—said to Rav Sheshet, 'And did Rav Huna [ר״ה] say thus?' etc. Hyman describes him as like a colleague of Rabbah, as in [Shabbat 108b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.108b.6): 'Rabbah and Rav Yosef bar Abba, who both said'; and in [Berakhot 11b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.11b.21), R' Abba (and in דק״ס: Rabbah) and R' Yosei bar Abba happened to come to a certain place; they asked them, 'What is the "one blessing"?' They did not have it in hand; they came

and asked Rav Matna; he did not have it in hand; they came and asked Rav Yehuda. Hyman cites Chullin 107 (compare [110a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.110a.2-4)), where he says that ר״ב and רי״בא disagree about the language in which R' Yitzchak bar Avdimi answered R' Elazar.

notes.text: ארי״בא is said Rav Yosef bar Abba by this entry’s full heading and connected chain. Carpenter/son of a carpenter is a metaphor for solving the difficult teaching, not occupational evidence.

The final Chullin107 exchange remains unmatched in the named107a/b text; ר״ב is unresolved. The abbreviation ר״ה in the Bava Metzia quotation also requires its actual paragraph. Hyman’s rival names and corrections remain distinct.

In the saved William Davidson vocalized Bava Metzia 72b paragraph, Rav Sheshet reports Rav Huna, and the question explicitly repeats Rav Huna; this supports the local expansion of ר״ה. That paragraph gives the alternative speaker as Rav Yosi bar Abba, distinct from Hyman’s supplied Rav Yosef bar Abba; neither name is harmonized. Hyman’s generation and colleague assessments, rival readings, and proposed Bava Kamma correction remain his claims. The other cited passages have not been freshly collated here, and abbreviated titles there remain R'. The final Chullin sigla ר״ב and רי״בא remain unresolved. The two preceding notes are preserved historical editorial notes; their earlier request for the Bava Metzia paragraph is qualified by this bounded comparison. No identity, chronology, or correction history is admitted.

Hyman’s printed notice (II, p. 750) cites Bava Batra 144b and Eruvin 7b, where the named texts contain the reports he describes. The supplied Hebrew has 145b and 6b. Bava Metzia 72b supports the mention of Rav Huna but gives Rav Yosi bar Abba as the alternative speaker, where Hyman has Rav Yosef. The printed Chullin 107 citation has no clear side marker. Chullin 110a has a close parallel. R’ Elazar is directed to Rav Yitzchak bar Avudimi, and the two versions of the reply are transmitted by Rav Kahana and R’ Yosi bar Abba. Hyman’s closing abbreviations remain as supplied. The parallel alone does not establish their expansion, identify Yosef with Yosi, or settle Hyman’s chronological and textual arguments. The specific editions cited for the other variant readings remain uncollated.

[Seder HaDorot 2027](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2027&lang=en) also proposes the change from bar Avahu to bar Abba at [Bava Kamma 112b:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.112b.8), and separately proposes Yosef for Yosei. In [Shabbat 108b:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.108b.6), Hyman and the linked text give Rabbah alongside Rav Yosef bar Abba, while Heilprin gives Rava. The readings carry different chronological implications.
